name: Personal Current Account Opening — Service Boundaries
description: Maps data model entities to owning service capabilities for JRN-001. Each service boundary section defines: owned entities, consumed APIs (synchronous inter-service calls), published events, and consumed events. Capabilities are the deployment boundary — a service owns its entities exclusively; no other service may write directly to another service's entities. All inter-service communication is via published API contracts or event bus (SVC-102).
architectural_principles: Single ownership: every entity is owned by exactly one service. No shared databases between services.
Capabilities as deployment boundary: a service is the unit of deployment and the unit of data ownership. The owning service is the only writer to its entities.
Share contracts not implementations: cross-service data access is always via a published API contract or event. No service reads another service's database directly.

Event-driven state propagation: domain events on SVC-102 (Event Bus) are the mechanism for communicating entity state changes between services. Synchronous APIs are used only where the calling service must block pending the result.
Compliance services (SVC-014, SVC-050, SVC-051) are hard blocking dependencies. Account provisioning cannot proceed without KYC clearance; KYC clearance cannot be granted without sanctions clearance.

owned_entities.ownership_rationale: SVC-001 is the authoritative retail ledger. Customer is the aggregate root of the Single Customer View (SCV) required by FSCS Depositor Protection rules. All downstream retail journeys (payments, savings, lending) reference customer identity from SVC-001. SCV maintenance — required for FSCS payout within 24 hours — must be co-located with the account ledger in a single transactional boundary.

SVC-001 is the retail ledger; the Account entity is a ledger record. Account creation (sort code/account number allocation, opening balance initialisation, FSCS SCV update) must be atomic within SVC-001. Splitting Account ownership from the ledger would make FSCS SCV consistency impossible to guarantee without distributed transactions.

CardIssuance tracks the bank's record of a card linked to an Account. As a ledger-adjacent entity owned by SVC-001, it participates in the FSCS SCV and the card lifecycle management that SVC-001 orchestrates with the card processor (Marqeta/Thredd). Card status changes (e.g. freeze following a compliance event on the Account) are applied atomically with account status changes.

ApplicationRecord reaches its terminal state when an Account is created in SVC-001. Co-locating ApplicationRecord in SVC-001 ensures transactional consistency between application approval and account provisioning. The decision_basis_ref and decline_reason in ApplicationRecord are the Consumer Duty evidence record — retained alongside the account ledger for the same 6–7 year period.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-001 calls SVC-050 to initiate identity verification and retrieve the KYCClearanceGranted or KYCReferralRaised result before creating an Account record. This is a blocking synchronous call: SVC-001 will not transition ApplicationRecord.status to 'approved' or create an Account without a KYCClearanceGranted event from SVC-050.
consumed_apis.governance_note: MLR 2017 Regulation 27: no business relationship may be established before CDD is complete. This API dependency is the technical enforcement of that obligation.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-001 consumes the CustomerRiskScoreUpdated event from SVC-014 to adjust account-level monitoring thresholds. This is an asynchronous event subscription — it does not block account creation but allows SVC-001 to maintain risk-aligned controls throughout the account lifecycle.
consumed_apis.governance_note: pKYC: SVC-001 must reflect updated risk tiers in account controls. Non-blocking because pKYC events occur post-onboarding.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-001 calls SVC-100 for customer authentication in online and mobile banking sessions (read account data, initiate transactions). Not required at account creation time — used from PH-006 onwards when the customer accesses the account.
consumed_apis.governance_note: PSR 2017 Regulation 100 SCA compliance: account access must be gated by SCA-compliant authentication from SVC-100.

published_events.trigger: PER-001 submits application form in PH-001; ApplicationRecord created with status = in_progress
Automated decision engine in PH-004 produces Approve/Refer/Decline outcome
published_events.payload_summary: application_id, customer_id, decision_outcome (approved|declined|referred), decision_basis_ref, decline_reason (internal, omitted if approved), referral_reason (internal, omitted if not referred), decided_at

published_events.trigger: Account record created in SVC-001 with status = pending in PH-005
published_events.payload_summary: account_id, customer_id, account_type, sort_code, account_number, iban, bic, opened_date, fscs_eligible

published_events.trigger: Account record transitions to status = active in PH-005 (SCV updated, CASS registration initiated)
published_events.payload_summary: account_id, customer_id, sort_code, account_number, status (active), cass_registered, provisioned_at

published_events.trigger: CardIssuance record created in PH-005 and CardIssuanceTriggered event dispatched to card processor
published_events.payload_summary: card_id, account_id, customer_id, card_type, issued_date, delivery_address (no PAN)
published_events.governance_note: PCI DSS: payload must not contain PAN or CVV2. Card processor (Marqeta/Thredd) produces the card number within its own PCI DSS-compliant environment.

consumed_events.purpose: Gates account provisioning. SVC-001 will not create an Account record without receiving this event. Triggers transition of ApplicationRecord.current_phase to PH-005.
Transitions ApplicationRecord.status to 'referred' and current_phase to AP-001. Account provisioning is suspended pending manual EDD completion.
Adjusts account-level monitoring thresholds in SVC-001 to reflect an updated KYC risk tier. Non-blocking post-onboarding event.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-001 owns both Customer and ApplicationRecord, even though ApplicationRecord spans all phases and SVC-017 is the channel-facing orchestrator of the application flow.
design_decisions.rationale: ApplicationRecord.status = 'approved' and the subsequent Account creation must be atomic within SVC-001 to ensure FSCS SCV consistency and prevent the edge case of an approved application without a corresponding account record. SVC-017 holds only presentation-layer flow state; SVC-001 holds the authoritative outcome.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: ApplicationRecord in SVC-017 (rejected: introduces distributed transaction risk between application approval and account creation); ApplicationRecord in SVC-050 (rejected: SVC-050 scope is CDD orchestration, not the full application lifecycle).

design_decisions.decision: SVC-001 does not own IdentityVerification or KycAssessment. It receives events from SVC-050 and SVC-014 but does not hold copies of CDD records.
design_decisions.rationale: CDD record ownership must remain with the MLRO-governed services (SVC-050 and SVC-014) for regulatory audit trail integrity. Duplicating CDD data into SVC-001 would create two systems of record for the same compliance obligation, violating the single-ownership principle and complicating FCA/NCA record production requests.

owned_entities.ownership_rationale: SVC-014 is the MLRO-governed KYC/AML service. KycAssessment is the CDD record of authority — it contains the PEP screening result, sanctions screening result (persisted from SVC-051's API response), adverse media result, risk tier, and MLRO sign-off. Ownership by SVC-014 ensures a single system of record for all CDD data under MLRO governance. FCA/NCA requests for CDD records are satisfied by a single service with a clean audit trail.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-014 calls SVC-051 synchronously to obtain the sanctions screening result for a customer being onboarded. The result is persisted in KycAssessment.sanctions_screening_result. If SVC-051 returns 'blocked', SVC-014 publishes SanctionsHitDetected and suspends the KYC assessment.
consumed_apis.governance_note: GOV-005-R02: real-time sanctions screening is mandatory. Batch-end or deferred screening is not compliant per OFSI obligation (Starling Bank FCA fine precedent). Hard limit: must return within 3,000ms (nfr.json PH-003 sanctions_screening_hard_limit_ms).

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-014 receives the IdentityVerificationCompleted event from SVC-050 to obtain the verified identity data (name, DOB, address, nationality) needed as inputs to PEP/sanctions/adverse media screening. SVC-014 does not call SVC-050 directly in synchronous mode — it subscribes to the event.
consumed_apis.governance_note: MLR 2017 Regulation 27: KYC/CDD may only proceed once identity verification is complete. The event subscription enforces this sequencing.

published_events.trigger: KycAssessment completed with risk_category = standard or simplified, pep_screening_result.status = clear, sanctions_screening_result.status = clear, and assessor = automated (or manual with mlro_sign_off recorded for AP-001 path)
published_events.payload_summary: assessment_id, customer_id, risk_category, assessment_date, next_review_date, assessor
published_events.governance_note: This event is the gating signal for SVC-001 to proceed with account provisioning. No account may be created without this event.

published_events.trigger: KycAssessment returns risk_category = enhanced, or pep_screening_result.status = match, or adverse_media_result.severity = high
published_events.payload_summary: assessment_id, customer_id, referral_reason (pep_identified | high_risk_score | adverse_media | edd_required), raised_at
published_events.governance_note: PER-052 (Compliance Officer / MLRO) is notified immediately. EDD (AP-001 path) must be completed before KYCClearanceGranted can be published.

published_events.trigger: KycAssessment receives a 'blocked' result from SVC-051 (sanctions_screening_result.status = blocked)
published_events.governance_note: GOV-005-R02: MLRO must be alerted immediately. OFSI notification within 14 days of confirmed designated person identification. Tipping-off prohibition (POCA 2002 s333A): payload must not be surfaced to PER-001.

published_events.trigger: pKYC periodic review results in a changed risk_category or risk_score for an existing customer (post-onboarding; not a JRN-001 event but published by SVC-014 throughout the relationship)
published_events.payload_summary: assessment_id, customer_id, previous_risk_category, new_risk_category, risk_score, updated_at

consumed_events.purpose: Signals that identity verification is complete with outcome = pass. SVC-014 uses the event payload (verified name, DOB, address, nationality) as inputs to PEP/sanctions/adverse media screening.
When SVC-051 updates its sanctions list data (e.g. new OFSI designations), SVC-014 triggers batch rescreening of the existing customer portfolio against the updated lists.

design_decisions.decision: KycAssessment stores the sanctions_screening_result (produced by SVC-051) as a field within the entity owned by SVC-014, rather than SVC-051 owning a separate entity.
design_decisions.rationale: SVC-051 is a stateless screening API. It does not persist results — it returns a synchronous screening decision. SVC-014 is the persistence owner of all CDD data. Giving SVC-051 its own entity would require SVC-014 to join across service boundaries to assemble the complete CDD record, violating the single-ownership principle.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: SVC-051 owns a SanctionsCheckRecord entity and SVC-014 references it by ID (rejected: creates cross-service FK, which is an anti-pattern in the share-contracts architecture; SVC-051 would become a persistence service rather than a stateless screening API).

design_decisions.decision: SVC-014 owns KycAssessment rather than SVC-050 (Customer Onboarding Service), even though SVC-050 orchestrates the onboarding flow.
design_decisions.rationale: MLRO governance accountability (POCA 2002, MLR 2017) attaches to the CDD record. The MLRO's system of record is SVC-014. SVC-050 is an orchestration service; it coordinates the flow but does not own the CDD outcome. Placing KycAssessment in SVC-050 would give a cross-cutting shared service ownership of a compliance-classified entity that requires MLRO-specific access controls and a 5+ year retention policy enforced independently of the onboarding flow.

owned_entities.ownership_rationale: SVC-050 is the Customer Onboarding Service that orchestrates identity verification (Onfido/Jumio). The IdentityVerification entity is the CDD document check record owned by SVC-050 under MLRO governance. SVC-050 calls the identity verification vendor, receives the result, persists it in IdentityVerification, and publishes IdentityVerificationCompleted. It is the single source of truth for document and biometric check outcomes. FCA/NCA requests for identity verification records (required within 2 business days per nfr.json PH-002 regulatory_sla) are satisfied from SVC-050.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-050 calls SVC-051 as the first step of the onboarding check sequence (before SVC-014 full KYC assessment). This is a preliminary sanctions pre-check: KYCClearanceGranted cannot be issued without a sanctions CLEAR result. In practice, SVC-050 orchestrates the call to SVC-051 and passes the result to SVC-014 for persistence in KycAssessment.
consumed_apis.governance_note: MLR 2017 and OFSI: sanctions screening is a blocking prerequisite. No identity verification outcome can be used to proceed to account opening without a sanctions CLEAR result.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-050 triggers SVC-014 to initiate the KYC/CDD assessment once identity verification is complete. SVC-050 passes verified identity data from IdentityVerification to SVC-014. This is an event-driven trigger — SVC-050 publishes IdentityVerificationCompleted and SVC-014 subscribes to begin the CDD assessment.
consumed_apis.governance_note: MLR 2017 Regulation 27: CDD must follow identity verification. The event-driven pattern enforces this sequencing.

published_events.trigger: SVC-050 receives result from identity verification vendor and persists IdentityVerification entity with a terminal outcome (pass | refer | fail | fraud_detected)
published_events.payload_summary: verification_id, customer_id, document_type, verification_provider, outcome, verification_timestamp
published_events.governance_note: Payload must not include raw document images, document_number, or biometric_match_score — only the outcome. Raw data remains within SVC-050's encrypted storage under MLR 2017 Regulation 40 5-year retention.

consumed_events.purpose: Signals that a new application has been initiated. SVC-050 uses the event payload (application_id, customer_id, channel) to initialise the identity verification workflow for the customer.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-050 is a cross-cutting shared service (SSC-001) owned by CAP-005 (Compliance & Regulatory), consumed by CAP-001 (Retail Banking), CAP-002 (Commercial Banking), and CAP-006 (Wealth). Its ownership of IdentityVerification ensures a single MLRO-accountable identity verification record regardless of which product capability initiated the onboarding.
design_decisions.rationale: Shared service resolution per shared-sub-capabilities.json SSC-001: 'The architectural principle (share contracts not implementations) is satisfied: CAP-001 and CAP-002 each own their product-specific account creation logic but both depend on the SVC-050 contract for identity verification and risk scoring.' Fragmented ownership would produce divergent verification standards across capabilities with different MLRO governance chains.

design_decisions.decision: Document images (from Onfido/Jumio) are stored in SVC-054 (Document Store — encrypted cold storage) referenced from IdentityVerification.verification_id, not stored as fields within the IdentityVerification entity.
design_decisions.rationale: UK GDPR Article 9 (special category biometric data) and MLR 2017 Regulation 40 (5-year CDD record retention) apply different access and security controls to document images versus outcome metadata. Storing images in a dedicated access-controlled document store (SVC-054) with its own encryption and audit log allows the two obligations to be managed independently, satisfying data minimisation (Article 5(1)(c)) for the main entity.

owned_entities.ownership_rationale: SVC-017 is the Digital Channels service responsible for the online and mobile banking experience. DigitalEnrollment is the channel activation record — it tracks credential creation status, biometric SCA enrolment status, device registration, and notification preferences for each customer's digital access. This metadata is native to the channel layer and is required by SVC-017 to manage session state, SCA enforcement, and push notification routing. The credential store itself is in SVC-100 (IAM); SVC-017 owns only the enrolment metadata.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-017 calls SVC-100 to: (1) create customer credentials (hashed password) in PH-006; (2) register the FIDO2/WebAuthn device and biometric enrolment assertion; (3) verify SCA authentication on first login. SVC-017 does not store credentials — it delegates all credential management to SVC-100.
consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous (blocking — credential creation and SCA verification must complete before DigitalChannelActivated event is published)
consumed_apis.governance_note: PSR 2017 Regulation 100: SCA enrolment must be complete before digital channel access is granted. GOV-001-R04.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-017 reads Account data (sort code, account number, account type, balance) from SVC-001 to render the PH-007 welcome dashboard. This is a read-only consumption — SVC-017 does not write to SVC-001 entities. SVC-017 also sends push notification and email communication triggers on domain events received from SVC-001.
consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous read (dashboard rendering); Asynchronous event subscription (for notifications)
consumed_apis.governance_note: Consumer Duty (PS22/9): welcome dashboard must display accurate account details immediately post-provisioning.

consumed_apis.api_description: SVC-017 calls SVC-053 to dispatch all customer-facing communications: in-app messages, push notifications, and email. In PH-007, SVC-017 instructs SVC-053 to dispatch the welcome pack (including the FSCS information sheet) within 15 minutes of the DigitalChannelActivated event.
consumed_apis.governance_note: GOV-001-R02: FSCS information sheet delivery at account opening is a mandatory regulatory disclosure. If SVC-053 is unavailable, the bank must have a fallback delivery mechanism — failure to deliver the FSCS information sheet at account opening is a regulatory breach.

published_events.trigger: DigitalEnrollment.status transitions to 'active' after first-login SCA authentication is confirmed in PH-006
published_events.payload_summary: enrollment_id, customer_id, channel, sca_factor, biometric_enrolled, enrolled_at
published_events.governance_note: This event signals the completion of the account opening journey for JRN-001. SVC-053 uses it to trigger the welcome pack dispatch (PH-007). SVC-001 uses it to confirm the account is operationally accessible.

published_events.trigger: SVC-017 confirms delivery of welcome email and in-app message (including FSCS information sheet) in PH-007
published_events.governance_note: GOV-001-R02: mandatory FSCS information sheet delivery. The event is the Consumer Duty evidence that the disclosure was made. Retained in SVC-111 (WORM) for 5 years.

consumed_events.purpose: SVC-017 uses this event to initialise the application flow UI and display the provisional application reference to PER-001.
SVC-017 advances the application wizard from PH-002 to PH-003 holding screen on receipt of this event (outcome = pass). For fail outcomes, SVC-017 displays the retry or branch referral message.
SVC-017 advances the UI from PH-003 holding screen to PH-004 decision result screen.
SVC-017 displays the 'additional review required' message to PER-001 with the 3-business-day SLA and case reference. Triggers SVC-053 to dispatch the referral notification email.
SVC-017 displays the generic decline message to PER-001 without disclosing the sanctions match (tipping-off prohibition). Triggers SVC-053 to dispatch the standard decline email.
SVC-017 renders the decision result screen (approval confirmation, referral status, or decline notification with FOS signpost).
SVC-017 advances the UI to the account details confirmation screen in PH-005.
SVC-017 confirms sort code and account number are live and advances to PH-006 digital channel activation setup.
SVC-017 displays the estimated card delivery date in PH-005/PH-007 and triggers the card dispatch notification via SVC-053.

design_decisions.decision: DigitalEnrollment is owned by SVC-017 (Digital Channels) rather than SVC-100 (Identity & Access Management). SVC-100 holds the authoritative credential store; SVC-017 holds the channel-layer enrolment metadata.
design_decisions.rationale: The split separates concerns: SVC-100 is a T0 foundation platform service responsible for security-critical credential management across all capabilities; SVC-017 is a T3 domain extension service responsible for the digital banking channel experience. Placing DigitalEnrollment in SVC-100 would conflate the security platform with channel-specific onboarding metadata (biometric_consent_recorded_at, push_notification_token, enrollment status for this specific journey). The two services operate at different tiers and release cadences.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-017 does not own any entities from ENT-001 through ENT-005. It reads account and customer data from SVC-001 via API and renders it to PER-001. SVC-017 is a channel and presentation service, not a data-owning domain service for banking entities.
design_decisions.rationale: Consistent with the architectural principle 'share contracts not implementations'. SVC-017's role is to compose the customer-facing experience from data owned by domain services. Duplication of Customer, Account, or ApplicationRecord data into SVC-017 would create stale read models and introduce consistency risks between the channel layer and the authoritative ledger.

service_boundaries.owned_entities_note: SVC-051 owns no entities in the JRN-001 data model. It is a stateless synchronous screening API. The sanctions_screening_result produced by SVC-051 is persisted within KycAssessment.sanctions_screening_result (owned by SVC-014). SVC-051 does not maintain a separate persistence store for individual screening results — it delegates result persistence to the calling KYC/AML service.

consumed_apis.api_description: Every screening decision (CLEAR / BLOCKED / PENDING_REVIEW) is immutably logged to SVC-103 and subsequently archived to SVC-111 (WORM store). This is a hard dependency: OFSI requires an audit log of all sanctions screening decisions. SVC-051 writes the screening audit record directly to SVC-103 on every screening call.
consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous write (non-blocking to the screening call — fire-and-forget to SVC-103 after result returned to caller)
consumed_apis.governance_note: GOV-005-R02: all screening decisions must be retained for 5 years for OFSI audit purposes (nfr.json PH-003 security_notes).

published_events.trigger: SVC-051 receives an updated sanctions list from ComplyAdvantage / Refinitiv World-Check (OFSI, OFAC, UN, EU lists refreshed). May occur at any time including outside business hours.
published_events.payload_summary: update_id, lists_updated (array of list names), updated_at, record_count_delta
published_events.governance_note: SVC-014 subscribes to this event to trigger portfolio batch rescreening. OFSI emergency designations must be reflected in screening results within the update latency window — typically minutes.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-051 has no owned entities in the JRN-001 data model. It is a stateless screening API that returns a synchronous result and logs to SVC-103. It does not persist per-customer screening records.
design_decisions.rationale: Consistent with the shared-sub-capabilities.json SSC-002 resolution: 'The service contract is the ownership mechanism — SVC-051 publishes a synchronous screening API.' Keeping SVC-051 stateless maximises its availability and simplifies its deployment model. No state means no data consistency obligations between screening calls — the caller (SVC-014) is responsible for persisting the result in the KycAssessment entity. This is critical for meeting the 3,000ms hard limit required by GOV-005-R02.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-051 logs every screening decision to SVC-103 directly, even though it does not own a persistence entity. This creates an audit trail in SVC-103/SVC-111 that is independent of whether SVC-014 successfully persisted the result in KycAssessment.
design_decisions.rationale: OFSI requires a complete audit log of screening decisions including those where the consuming service subsequently failed to persist the result. A two-writer audit pattern (SVC-051 writes the raw screening log; SVC-014 writes the assessed CDD record) provides defence-in-depth for the regulatory audit trail. The SVC-103 record is the ground truth for OFSI compliance purposes.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-051 operates in an active-active multi-region configuration with no degraded mode. Account openings are blocked — not queued, not skipped — during any SVC-051 outage.
design_decisions.rationale: GOV-005-R02 and the Starling Bank FCA enforcement precedent (£29m fine, October 2024 for incomplete sanctions screening coverage). There is no compliant degraded mode for sanctions screening — the bank cannot open accounts while the screening service is unavailable. Circuit-breaker must halt account openings, not bypass screening (nfr.json PH-003 degraded_mode note).

cross_service_interaction_summary.description: End-to-end event and API flow across service boundaries for the JRN-001 happy path, in phase order.

interaction_sequence.description: PER-001 submits application. SVC-017 calls SVC-001 to create Customer (prospect) and ApplicationRecord. SVC-001 publishes ApplicationStarted.

SVC-050 receives ApplicationStarted. Orchestrates identity verification via Onfido/Jumio. Creates IdentityVerification entity. Calls SVC-051 for preliminary sanctions pre-check. Publishes IdentityVerificationCompleted (outcome=pass).

SVC-014 subscribes to IdentityVerificationCompleted. Calls SVC-051 for full sanctions screening (blocking, 3,000ms hard limit). Performs PEP and adverse media screening via ComplyAdvantage/Refinitiv. Creates KycAssessment entity. Publishes KYCClearanceGranted.

SVC-001 subscribes to KYCClearanceGranted. Automated decision engine runs. ApplicationRecord.status transitions to 'approved'. SVC-001 publishes ApplicationDecisionMade (APPROVED). SVC-017 renders approval confirmation to PER-001.

SVC-001 creates Account entity (sort code/account number allocated). Updates Customer.status to 'active'. Updates FSCS SCV. Creates CardIssuance entity. Publishes AccountOpened, AccountProvisioned, CardIssuanceTriggered.
SVC-017 receives AccountProvisioned. Guides PER-001 through credential creation and biometric SCA enrolment (calls SVC-100). Creates DigitalEnrollment entity. Publishes DigitalChannelActivated.

SVC-017 receives DigitalChannelActivated. Renders welcome dashboard (reads Account from SVC-001). Calls SVC-053 to dispatch welcome pack (email + in-app, FSCS information sheet). Publishes WelcomePackDispatched.
